main_argument_chains.claim: The baseline keep-right-except-to-pass rule is not optimal under the source's five metrics.
support_steps: Criteria and directions are defined on p5-p6.
Light and heavy analyses produce distinct baseline failure mechanisms on p7-p11.
CA curves and screenshots provide model-internal checks on p17-p19.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The paper is justified in designing alternatives rather than treating the existing rule as fixed.

main_argument_chains.claim: New Rule 2 is the selected option under the stated CA scenario and AHP weights.
support_steps: Rules 1-3 encode distinct interventions on p20-p21.
p22-p24 normalize directions, disclose the matrix, and pass CR.
Table 9 gives Rule 2 the largest EIC.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The recommendation is conditional on the displayed metrics, parameter setting, and author preferences.

main_argument_chains.claim: Orientation and automation conclusions are extensions rather than unconditional universal claims.
support_steps: p25 names right-side and human-judgment assumptions.
p26 mirrors lane orientation for LHT.
p27 changes controller information and action conditions.
p28 compares IDS outputs by lambda.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Future use must preserve or retest the changed assumptions and displayed regime conditions.

warnings.warning: The prose sets T=1000 seconds while Figure 8 initializes T=2000; the experiment horizon is contradictory.
Table 5 uses lambda=.25 but p25 says this section arbitrarily used lambda=.3 before claiming .2/.4 robustness.
The shortened observation denominator permits TF to exceed source arrival rate, so it is not directly a steady-state conservation throughput.
ATS units are not reconciled among km/h definitions, m/s examples, cells, and approximately 3.2-4.0 reported values.
Text compares speed difference to L m/s, while Figure 9 uses a +1 cell comparison without explaining scale equivalence.
SI=1/(1+DI) makes zero-lane-change Rule 2 automatically perfect by construction and omits other safety mechanisms.
The prose predicts IDS ATS becomes worse in heavy traffic, but Figure 20 keeps IDS above non-IDS over its displayed lambda range.
IDS heavy-state discussion cites subsection 3.1 although the relevant heavy analysis is 3.3.
LHT orientation transfer has no independent CA, AHP, or empirical rerun despite a safety conclusion.
One-factor tables do not establish coupled uncertainty, stochastic repeatability, or rule-winner stability.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Four visual Summary paragraphs establish baseline diagnosis, CA cross-check, AHP selection, extension, and public recommendation.
Logic framework maps four tasks to criteria, theory, CA, new rules, AHP, LHT, and IDS.
Following-versus-overtaking diagram provides the local behavioral mechanism for the transition model.
Displayed state-transition matrix connects speed-state proportions and overtaking probabilities.
Numerical state-proportion plot reaches the claimed lowest-speed absorbing state.
Heavy-traffic lane diagram depicts v3 queueing on the right, v4 left-lane occupancy, and safe distance.
Two-by-S CA grid shows lane rows, entrance, cell scale, and forward direction.
Go-process sketch specifies forward and rear left-lane safety windows.
Return-process sketch specifies the right-lane safety window.
Main simulation flowchart exposes initialization, repeated update, and output stages.
Go-process subflowchart exposes safety checks, deceleration, and p1/p2 branch logic.
Baseline CA outputs at lambda 0.25 and 0.4 instantiate five evaluation criteria.
Danger-index curve versus lambda supports the stated nonmonotonic interpretation.
Average-speed curve versus lambda supports the decreasing-load interpretation.
Traffic-flow curve versus lambda supports the capacity-saturation narrative.
OSL-effect curve records high-limit response across arrival rate.
USL-effect curve records low-limit response across arrival rate.
Light-traffic screenshot visually checks right-lane concentration predicted by the state model.
Heavy-traffic screenshot visualizes left-lane trapping and practical rule failure.
p1 sensitivity table reports relative movement in five criteria.
p2 sensitivity table reports relative movement in five criteria.
d sensitivity table reports relative movement in five criteria.
Raw five-criterion comparison gives the old rule and three new-rule inputs to selection.
Normalized indices make four rules comparable across five criteria.
Radar chart gives a provisional multi-criterion comparison before AHP aggregation.
Saaty scale makes the verbal AHP preference encoding inspectable.
Five-by-five matrix is the reproducible input to the reported weights and consistency statistics.
AHP weight vector documents the tradeoff encoded in the comprehensive index.
Comprehensive EIC table gives the Rule 2 selection result.
LHT/RHT layout shows the claimed orientation mirror for the no-overtaking rule.
Four paired IDS/non-IDS curves compare traffic flow, ATS, USL, and OSL across lambda.
